and_the_consumer_is_proven_not_assumed.the_change: ot_a3_microsequencer takes DEP_CHECK_STAGES and owes the table one more cycle at depth 2, in BOTH consumers -- the range scan and the predicate hazard.  The owed count is a comparison rather than a part-select of the integer parameter, because the depth campaign records that indexing a part-select is accepted by one of the two simulators and rejected by the other.
and_the_consumer_is_proven_not_assumed.the_gate: tools/rtl_abi3_dep_check_depth_campaign.py replays the WHOLE ABI 3.0 vector set through the real control plane at both depths under both simulators, and requires the marker the vector set derives from its golden execution on runtime.sim.device.Device
and_the_consumer_is_proven_not_assumed.what_was_missing: rtl/test/tb_a3_dependence_table_depth.sv proved the TABLE: depth 2 equals depth 1 delayed by one cycle, 20,000 cycles, both simulators.  It says nothing about the microsequencer, whose hazard scan is pipelined -- each cycle issues a check pair and folds in the previous cycle's results -- so at depth 2 the last pair's answer arrives after the loop has left.  Dropping it would issue an instruction over a live hazard: a silent wrong answer, not a stall.
